extracted.intended_audience: researchers (authors and reviewers), journal editors, and platform adopters interested in pre-journal peer review (Review Commons)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for conducting and using journal-agnostic peer review of manuscripts and preprints via the Review Commons platform, including reviewer expectations, editorial selection, public posting of reports, and affiliated journal practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-agnostic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Disentangle the review process from the context of a specific journal so reviewers focus on the science rather than journal-specific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are encouraged to write reports that are portable and objective. This promotes reviews that evaluate the scientific merits independently of a given journal's editorial 'bar' and should make reviews more useful across journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate the work 'as is'
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting additional experiments, reviewers are asked to evaluate the work 'as is' and not as it would have to be in order to meet the editorial 'bar' of a given journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constrains requests for extra work to what is necessary to judge the current manuscript, avoiding demands motivated solely by meeting higher-impact journal expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of significance in context
rubrics_metrics.description: Review can include an expert assessment of the significance of the study for the field by placing it in the context of the existing literature and assessing the nature of the reported advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should go beyond technical checks and offer informed judgements about the study's contribution and novelty relative to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific evaluation: scrutinize evidence and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is a scientific activity where interpretations can be challenged, evidence scrutinized and findings compared to preexisting knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should provide substantiated, critical, and constructive scientific analysis that examines methodology, data interpretation, and consistency with the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial editorial selection for platform review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Managing Editor carries out an initial editorial assessment (with an academic advisory board) to select manuscripts that fall within the scientific scope of the platform and that represent a significant advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is constrained by scope and a requirement that submissions 'represent a significant advance: that is they are of concrete value for a specific scientific community.' Not all preprints will be accepted for Review Commons review due to resource limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality, substantiated reviewer reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be high-quality: substantiated, critical, and constructive scientific analyses typically produced by multiple expert reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial notes that one round of review typically involves three researchers each spending ~6 hours; reviewers should provide detailed, evidence-based comments that help authors improve strength and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of Refereed Preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are invited to make the full set of reviews and their response publicly available as 'Refereed Preprints' on bioRxiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting Refereed Preprints provides unfiltered and transparent access to in-depth analyses by independent experts and avoids forcing a binary accepted/rejected outcome onto review results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer and authentication of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons transfers the manuscript, the reviews, and the authors' response to bioRxiv and to target journals directly on behalf of the authors, thereby authenticating them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This direct transfer streamlines submission and ensures provenance of referee reports for journals and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliated journals' commitments and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals affiliated with Review Commons have agreed not to review manuscripts afresh, although they may ask for additional advice to arbitrate issues or seek complementary expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliated journals are encouraged to only re-contact original referees if required for an informed editorial process and not to request an editorial opinion on journal fit; there is no tie-in and authors may withdraw or choose other journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee name sharing only with consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of referees will be shared with journals only with explicit referee consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer identity is controlled by consent, preserving referee privacy unless they agree to disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of scientific assessment and editorial decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific and editorial evaluations are distinct tasks: scientific assessment should focus on the quality and interpretation of the work, while editorial decisions concern journal fit and acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separating these tasks aims to increase transparency and efficiency by preventing conflation of scientific critique with journal-selection judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge resource and scalability limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The platform recognizes finite reviewer availability and that providing in-depth reviews for every preprint is unlikely in the near term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Commons uses editorial triage and a scalable system design, and will collect evidence on uptake and operational variables to adapt policies and sustainability models over time.
